steps.name: Effective-Edge Curve
steps.detail: PROFILE LIMBO-19, judged against the RTP-CLAIM band (0.1 pp from the 1.00% edge claim) on the current build's target range, 1.01x to the 10000x ceiling seen on the live API on 2026-09-26 (one request above it probed, not settled — Step 25): 0 of the 999900 targets sit more than the band from the claim (no FLAG); inside the band the derived edge differs from the 1.00% claim at 999618 of the 999900 targets, always on the house side, by at most 0.009982 pp (1.009982% at 9989.91x) — printed, not flagged. The first legal target beyond the band is 100101.12x (RTP 98.899907%). NOT THE CURRENT BUILD, disclosed for reference: on the 2026-09-11 range (targets up to 500000x, the highest target the audited capture settled; 49999900 targets) the worst edge is 1.497487% at 497487.44x and the RTP-CLAIM rule would FAIL: 23885381 of the 49999900 targets sit more than 0.1 pp below the claim, worst RTP 98.502513% at 497487.44x; over the whole declared legal grid the edge differs from the claim at 99999490 of 99999900 targets, up to 1.989999%. EXHAUSTIVE over the legal grid: house edge >= 1.00% asserted in EXACT INTEGERS (floor(9900000000/ci(m)) x ci(m) <= 9900000000, no tolerance) at EVERY one of the 99999900 legal 2-dp targets in [1.01x, 1000000x] — 0 violations (the grid size is both what the legal window implies and the pinned population 99999900). THE EDGE IS NOT FLAT ABOVE 1.00%, and this is the measurement that says so: edge(ci) = (10000000000 - 9900000000 + (9900000000 mod ci)) / 10000000000, so the excess over 1% is driven by (N mod ci) and grows with ci. Worst edge anywhere in the legal range 1.989999% at 990000.01x; worst target playable on 2026-09-11 (<= 500000x, the $50000/$0.1 exposure ceiling of Step 17; on 2026-09-26 the live API did not settle the one target probed above 10000x, Step 25) 1.497487% at 497487.44x; worst at or below the operator's UI target cap of 10000x 1.009982% at 9989.91x; the FIRST target whose edge exceeds 1.01% is 10009.10x (1.010001%), i.e. just above that UI cap; 94389859 of the 99999900 legal targets carry an edge above 1.01%, and only 410 are priced at EXACTLY 1.00% (those are the ci that divide 9900000000 evenly); mechanically it is a same-odds/different-payout effect — targets sharing one value of floor(N/ci) share an IDENTICAL win chance but are each paid their own multiplier, so within a group RTP = cr x ci / 10000000000 rises with ci and only the LARGEST member is priced as well as those odds allow; every smaller member is strictly dominated (same win chance, strictly lower payout). Just 198798 of 99999900 targets (0.199%) are the best-priced member of their group. NOTE, because the obvious misreading is wrong: best-priced does NOT mean priced at 99.00% — only 410 targets in the whole grid are, so a group maximum is usually still above a 1.00% edge. CAPTURED-TARGET SUB-MEASUREMENT, reported separately and NOT to be read as the curve: across the 1104 distinct targets this capture actually used, spanning 1.01x..500000x, 0 violations, 0 player-favourable targets (none — not exploitable anywhere in the captured range); 0 targets at which OUR OWN reference formula returned a non-finite value (none — the curve above is a measurement of the pricing, not of a broken verifier), counted explicitly because every comparison against NaN is false and an unguarded curve would read as clean; captured edge spans 1.000000% (at 1.1x) to 1.000041% (at 43.86x), stake-weighted mean across the capture 1.000000% — that narrow span is an ARTEFACT OF WHICH TARGETS THE CAPTURE USED (every high tranche it played divides 9900000000 evenly), not a property of the game; 57 of the 1104 captured targets price to EXACTLY 1.00% (e.g. target 2.00 -> win chance 49.50%, RTP 99.0000%) — that is the arithmetic working, not an anomaly; the flooring can only LOWER the payout, never raise it, which is why 1.00% is a provable floor rather than a measured average, and why the dispersion above it runs one way only; legal-range extremes also satisfy the identity (1.01x, 500000x, 1000000x: ok), max win chance 98.019801% at the 1.01x minimum target; the comparison is done in integers, so no tolerance is needed; the largest edge on the captured targets is 1.00004134% at 43.86x, a real difference from 1.00% and not a rounding effect
